title: C# Questions & Answers - Interfaces Implementation
sourceFile: Interfaces Implementation - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on implementation of the interfaces in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What will be the Correct statement in the following C# code?

options.text: class a is an abstract class
A method table would not be created for class a
The definition of f1() in class a should be void a1.f1()
None of the mentioned

questions.explanation: Implicit interface implementation requires a public method. void f1() is private by default, so it does not implement a1.f1(). Use public void f1() or explicit void a1.f1().

questions.question: Choose the wrong statement about 'INTERFACE' in C#.NET?

options.text: An explicitly implemented member could be accessed from an instance of the interface
Interface members are public by default
An interface could not contain signature of the indexer
None of the mentioned

questions.explanation: Interfaces can declare indexers. Interface members are public by default, and explicitly implemented members are accessed through an interface reference.

questions.question: What will be the Correct statement in the following C# code?

options.text: Class a could not have an instance data
Class a should be declared abstract because it does not implement f2()
Class a fully implements the interface a1
None of the mentioned

questions.explanation: A non-abstract class must implement every interface member. Here f2() is missing, so the class must be declared abstract or it will not compile.

questions.question: What will be the Correct statement in the following C# code?

options.text: Functions should be declared inside an interface
It is workable code
Properties cannot be declared inside an interface
None of the mentioned

questions.explanation: The snippet is valid: an interface may declare properties and methods. Option c is false.

questions.question: What will be the correct way to implement the interface in the following C# code?

options.text: None of the mentioned

questions.explanation: None of a–c implements interface abc. They use the wrong type name (employee/person), Java implements, or a broken property. Correct would be class emp : abc { public string name { get; set; } } (or an explicit abc.name implementation).

questions.question: In order to avoid ambiguity among an interface derived from two base interfaces with same method name(and signature), the right code among the following C# codes is?

options.text: All of the mentioned

questions.explanation: When two interfaces declare the same method, the class implements each explicitly as void i1.m1() and void i2.m1(). Option a duplicates i1.m1; option b is not valid syntax.
